name: Graph-Based Geolocation
problem_statement: Infer geographic coordinates for unlocated vertices using declared graph propagation or supervised graph-learning models.

normalization: Preserve all declared vertices, including isolated vertices.
Preserve direction; an undirected projection must be explicitly requested.
Declare the treatment of self-loops and parallel edges before execution; an adapter must reject unsupported cases.

problem_inputs.name: method_family
problem_inputs.description: Distinguish spatial-median propagation from learned geographic regression on attributed graphs.

problem_inputs.name: seed_locations
problem_inputs.description: Known latitude/longitude coordinates keyed by vertex.

problem_inputs.name: method_definition
problem_inputs.description: Propagation objective, geographic metric, confidence thresholds and stopping conditions.

problem_inputs.name: training_definition
problem_inputs.description: Required for supervised_graph_learning: architecture, features, training/validation/test vertex split, target coordinate normalization, optimizer and stopping rule.

required_outputs.name: locations
required_outputs.description: Estimated coordinates or null for unresolved vertices.

required_outputs.name: confidence
required_outputs.description: Declared confidence or dispersion per estimated vertex.

required_outputs.name: converged
required_outputs.description: Whether the method stopping condition was met.

solution_semantics.objective: Optimize the explicitly declared geographic propagation objective or supervised geographic regression loss.
solution_semantics.exactness: Estimates are model-dependent; graph layout coordinates are not geographic predictions.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Output identities refer to the normalized input; any multiplicities must follow the declared task.
solution_semantics.ordering: No output order or choice among equally valid optima is required unless specified by an input.

validation_rules: Latitude and longitude are in valid ranges.
Evaluate geodesic error on held-out known locations without label leakage.
For learned methods, fit preprocessing on the training split and prevent held-out locations from entering node features.
Preserve known seeds in returned outputs when hold_seeds_fixed is true; training loss alone does not establish this property.
edge_cases: A component without located seeds may remain unresolved.
Geodesic distances account for the antimeridian.

correctness: Latitude and longitude are in valid ranges.
Evaluate geodesic error on held-out known locations without label leakage.
